news.title: 'I had to get the shock on my heart!' - Scott McTominay reveals secret hospital dash and cardiac procedure before Scotland's World Cup opener
news.lede: Scott McTominay has shared a startling revelation regarding his health, admitting he required an emergency heart procedure just 48 hours before Scotland’s World Cup opener. The Napoli midfielder was rushed to the hospital under police escort shortly after the national team arrived in the United States for their tournament campaign. The secret hospital dash in Boston Scotland international McTominay has finally broken his silence on a medical emergency that nearly derailed his participation in the World Cup this past June. While the public was told at the time that the midfielder was suffering from a minor illness, the reality was far more serious.

news.title: England’s 1966 World Cup winner’s medal to fetch $400,000 at auction
news.lede: Football legend Gordon Banks’ 1966 World Cup winner’s medal could fetch £300,000 ($405,000) at auction. The goalkeeper received the award after England beat West Germany 4-2 at Wembley on July 30, 1966. It comes in its original fitted case and was last sold at Christie’s in March 2001 as part of the Gordon Banks Collection. Estimated to fetch £220,000-£300,000 ($295,000-$405,000), the medal is among 164 lots in the Spink and Budds sale spanning more than three centuries of sporting history.

news.title: Scotland’s McTominay reveals World Cup heart scare
news.lede: Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay has revealed he had to have his heart shocked just two days before playing in his country’s World Cup opener against Haiti. McTominay was said to have missed training in the lead-up to the 1-0 victory over Haiti in Massachusetts due to a stomach complaint. But, speaking at a press conference in Glasgow on Tuesday, the 29-year-old said: “I had to go and get the shock on my heart two days before the Haiti game.” McTominay played in all three of Scotland’s matches at the World Cup, but was below his best as they exited at the group stage after losing to Morocco and Brazil.

news.title: World Cup trophy used by Messi in viral Instagram photo sells for $525,000
news.lede: The World Cup replica trophy held by Lionel Messi after Argentina's historic win over France at the 2022 tournament in Qatar sold for a staggering price. (Richmond Auctions via SWNS). A replica World Cup trophy used by Lionel Messi in an Instagram post that became the most-liked photo in the world has sold for a whopping £390,000 ($525,000). Argentina lifted the real solid gold trophy after squeezing past France on penalties during its historic campaign at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

news.title: Scott McTominay: Scotland midfielder had heart 'shocked' two days before World Cup opener against Haiti
news.lede: Scott McTominay has revealed he needed to have his heart “shocked” two days before Scotland's World Cup opener against Haiti. The Napoli midfielder underwent a cardiac ablation procedure in Manchester in September to treat a mild, benign heart arrhythmia that first came to light after the Scots arrived in the United States in early June and then continued to affect him in August while back in Italy playing for his club. At the time, the Scotland camp, clearly keen to keep McTominay's situation under wraps, said the 29-year-old had missed training in the lead-up to the World Cup due to a stomach complaint. news.title: Scotland vs North Macedonia: Scott McTominay reveals heart treatment at World Cup
news.lede: McTominay reveals he underwent heart procedure days before World Cup game. Scott McTominay says he received treatment to correct an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland's World Cup win over Haiti in June. The Napoli midfielder recently underwent an ablation procedure - a minimally invasive operation to correct irregular heart rhythms - in Manchester. At the World Cup, the 29-year-old was was put to sleep to correct his heartbeat and given the all-clear to play in the opening 1-0 victory over Haiti in Massachusetts.
